dimensions.assessment: Potentially affects all participants in the United States economy and monetary system by altering the legal goals of central bank policy.
dimensions.evidence: This bill removes maximum employment as a goal of the monetary policy set by the Board of Governors

dimensions.assessment: Alters the statutory mandate governing national monetary policy decisions, changing how the Federal Reserve balances employment and inflation.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Federal Reserve Act to remove the mandate on the Board of Governors... to focus on maximum employment.

dimensions.assessment: Does not appropriate federal spending or alter tax revenues directly, though it may influence broader economic conditions.
Modifies a single key section of the Federal Reserve Act concerning the statutory objectives of monetary policy.
dimensions.evidence: Section 2A of the Federal Reserve Act (12 U.S.C. 225a) is amended by striking maximum employment

dimensions.assessment: Provides a permanent statutory change to the operating mandate of the nation's central bank.

missing_information: Specific economic or interest rate impacts resulting from the removal of the employment mandate
importance_detail.rationale: The bill removes maximum employment as a monetary policy mandate for the Federal Reserve, leaving stable prices as the sole focus.
